Live checks for **VERSION**, using the packaged DeepSeek edition installed like a user would. An unchecked item means unverified.

### Before tagging

- [ ] Clean `npm ci` installs the locked Electron and Vite security updates; dependency audit passes.
- [ ] Source, lockfile, main and embedded extension versions agree; reviewed release notes and translated What's New exist.
- [ ] A fresh profile signs in to DeepSeek in the built-in browser without a tunnel, provider connector or external extension.
- [ ] An ordinary task runs a local tool, receives its exact result, and reaches a recorded final answer.
- [ ] Create plan returns a validated workflow from the real hidden helper; a failed or cancelled plan keeps the original draft.
- [ ] Goal stops at a small objective; Loop continues within its brief. Stop cancels the exact running turn.
- [ ] One worker runs a command and reports back; Compact & Resume preserves session identity and history.
- [ ] Activity reflects sign-in independently of legacy MCP state. Update checks do not connect a tunnel or refresh plugins.
- [ ] Usage says it is a local cost comparison, retains small decimal amounts, and preserves explicit rate overrides.
- [ ] Type checking, ordinary tests, `verify:ui`, notices and full Git-history privacy checks pass on the release source.
- [ ] All six native targets build and pass packaged-runtime checks. Linux DEB metadata and executable names belong to DeepSeek On Steroids.
- [ ] The fork's release, issue and security-report links are configured. No download or update points to the upstream app.
- [ ] Corresponding native sources, candidate provenance and SHA-256 checksums accompany the installers. No unrelated logs, private correspondence or runtime data enter the public source export.

### After publishing

- [ ] Published-asset verification passes, including tag/source provenance and every checksum.
- [ ] Install and exercise the downloaded packages; source tests alone do not establish installed behavior.
